rows.name: Continue
rows.description: The server has received the request headers and the client should proceed to send the request body.

rows.name: Switching Protocols
rows.description: The requester has asked the server to switch protocols and the server has agreed to do so.

rows.name: Processing
rows.description: The server has received and is processing the request, but no response is available yet.

rows.name: Early Hints
rows.description: Used to return some response headers before final HTTP message.

rows.name: OK
rows.description: The request succeeded. The meaning depends on the HTTP method used.

rows.name: Created
rows.description: The request succeeded and a new resource was created as a result.

rows.name: Accepted
rows.description: The request has been received but not yet acted upon.

rows.name: Non-Authoritative Information
rows.description: The returned metadata is not exactly the same as available from the origin server.

rows.name: No Content
rows.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

rows.name: Reset Content
rows.description: Tells the user agent to reset the document which sent this request.

rows.name: Partial Content
rows.description: Used when the Range header is sent from the client to request only part of a resource.

rows.name: Multi-Status
rows.description: Conveys information about multiple resources, for situations where multiple status codes might be appropriate.

rows.name: Already Reported
rows.description: Used inside a DAV: propstat response to avoid repeatedly enumerating the internal members.

rows.name: IM Used
rows.description: The server has fulfilled a GET request and the response is a representation of the result.

rows.name: Multiple Choices
rows.description: The request has more than one possible response. The user agent should choose one of them.

rows.name: Moved Permanently
rows.description: The URL of the requested resource has been changed permanently. The new URL is given in the response.

rows.name: Found
rows.description: The URI of requested resource has been changed temporarily. Further changes may be made in the future.

rows.name: See Other
rows.description: The server sent this response to direct the client to get the requested resource at another URI with a GET request.

rows.name: Not Modified
rows.description: Used for caching purposes. It tells the client that the response has not been modified.

rows.name: Use Proxy
rows.description: Deprecated. Was defined to indicate that a requested response must be accessed by a proxy.

rows.name: Temporary Redirect
rows.description: The server sends this response to direct the client to get the requested resource at another URI with same method.

rows.name: Permanent Redirect
rows.description: The resource is now permanently located at another URI, specified by the Location header.

rows.name: Bad Request
rows.description: The server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error.

rows.name: Unauthorized
rows.description: The client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

rows.name: Payment Required
rows.description: Reserved for future use. The original aim was for digital payment systems.

rows.name: Forbidden
rows.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; the server is refusing to give the requested resource.

rows.name: Not Found
rows.description: The server cannot find the requested resource. This can also mean the endpoint is valid but the resource does not exist.

rows.name: Method Not Allowed
rows.description: The request method is known by the server but is not supported by the target resource.

rows.name: Not Acceptable
rows.description: The server cannot produce a response matching the list of acceptable values defined in the request headers.

rows.name: Proxy Authentication Required
rows.description: Similar to 401 Unauthorized but authentication is needed to be done by a proxy.

rows.name: Request Timeout
rows.description: The server would like to shut down this unused connection.

rows.name: Conflict
rows.description: This response is sent when a request conflicts with the current state of the server.

rows.name: Gone
rows.description: The requested content has been permanently deleted from server, with no forwarding address.

rows.name: Length Required
rows.description: Server rejected the request because the Content-Length header field is not defined and the server requires it.

rows.name: Precondition Failed
rows.description: The client has indicated preconditions in its headers which the server does not meet.

rows.name: Payload Too Large
rows.description: Request entity is larger than limits defined by server.

rows.name: URI Too Long
rows.description: The URI requested by the client is longer than the server is willing to interpret.

rows.name: Unsupported Media Type
rows.description: The media format of the requested data is not supported by the server.

rows.name: Range Not Satisfiable
rows.description: The range specified by the Range header field in the request cannot be fulfilled.

rows.name: Expectation Failed
rows.description: The expectation indicated by the Expect request header field cannot be met by the server.

rows.name: I'm a Teapot
rows.description: The server refuses the attempt to brew coffee with a teapot.

rows.name: Misdirected Request
rows.description: The request was directed at a server that is not able to produce a response.

rows.name: Unprocessable Entity
rows.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed due to semantic errors.

rows.name: Locked
rows.description: The resource that is being accessed is locked.

rows.name: Failed Dependency
rows.description: The request failed due to failure of a previous request.

rows.name: Too Early
rows.description: Indicates that the server is unwilling to risk processing a request that might be replayed.

rows.name: Upgrade Required
rows.description: The server refuses to perform the request using the current protocol but might after the client upgrades.

rows.name: Precondition Required
rows.description: The origin server requires the request to be conditional.

rows.name: Too Many Requests
rows.description: The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time (rate limiting).

rows.name: Request Header Fields Too Large
rows.description: The server is unwilling to process the request because its header fields are too large.

rows.name: Unavailable For Legal Reasons
rows.description: The user agent requested a resource that cannot legally be provided.

rows.name: Internal Server Error
rows.description: The server has encountered a situation it does not know how to handle.

rows.name: Not Implemented
rows.description: The request method is not supported by the server and cannot be handled.

rows.name: Bad Gateway
rows.description: The server, while working as a gateway, got an invalid response needed to handle the request.

rows.name: Service Unavailable
rows.description: The server is not ready to handle the request. Common causes are maintenance or overload.

rows.name: Gateway Timeout
rows.description: The server is acting as a gateway and cannot get a response in time.

rows.name: HTTP Version Not Supported
rows.description: The HTTP version used in the request is not supported by the server.

rows.name: Variant Also Negotiates
rows.description: The server has an internal configuration error.

rows.name: Insufficient Storage
rows.description: The server is unable to store the representation needed to complete the request.

rows.name: Loop Detected
rows.description: The server detected an infinite loop while processing the request.

rows.name: Not Extended
rows.description: Further extensions to the request are required for the server to fulfill it.

rows.name: Network Authentication Required
rows.description: Indicates that the client needs to authenticate to gain network access.

key_takeaways: Download data in Excel, CSV, or PDF format.
Use ISO codes for easy integration with other systems.
use_cases: Import the **CSV** file into your database or use it with Python/pandas for data analysis.
Open the **Excel** file to filter, sort, and create Pivot Tables for quick insights.
Print the **PDF** version for offline reference or classroom handouts.
Use the data to build applications, dashboards, or educational resources.
